title: Exact and Approximate Algorithms for Polytree Learning
anchored_claims: The exact algorithm for finding an optimal polytree with bounded in-degree k runs in time O((2+epsilon)^n * |I|^O(1)) for arbitrarily small epsilon > 0 (Theorem 3.3).
This improves on the previously fastest known exact algorithm, which runs in time O(3^n * |I|^O(1)) matching Gruttemeier et al. (2021a) (Theorem 3.1).

A polynomial-time algorithm achieves a (k+1)-approximation to the optimal polytree score for arbitrary scoring functions with in-degree bound k, and this approximation ratio is shown near-optimal under the Unique Games Conjecture (Theorem 4.1).
For additive scoring functions, a polynomial-time algorithm achieves a 2-approximation to the optimal polytree score (Theorem 4.2).

The near-tightness of the (2+epsilon)^n exact-algorithm running time is established via a reduction from k'-Set Cover, showing no improvement below (2+epsilon)^n is possible under standard complexity assumptions (Theorem 3.5).
